chapter: Jelly Roll Morton and other records
title: Sidemen: Bud Scott, Johnny Lindsey and Roy Palmer
summary: He worked with banjoist and guitarist Bud Scott, Johnny Lindsey and trombonist Roy Palmer on other jobs, though he cannot place Scott on the Morton dates.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I think St. Cyr is on most of those, but I believe Bud Scott, do you remember? Did you record Bud Scott? Bud Scott, let's see. On banjo or guitar or some of them? Seems to me like Bud Scott was with, now was he with us when, with Lil, when we recorded with Lil? I think St. Cyr was on that date, I'm pretty sure. I think he said, he's heard those and told me that. But I think some of those with Johnny Dodds with Jelly Roll and Baby Dodds, I believe maybe, doesn't sound like the banjo that St. Cyr, I think it might have been Bud Scott's guitar. Bud Scott, yeah. Uh-huh. I just wondered if you remembered. No, I, I can't remember, but I remember making a recording with somebody.

I worked with Bud. Because I worked with Bud quite a bit around here. Oh, with Jimmy Noon, was he with you then too? Yes, no, he was with, with me down here with Dave Payton had a band in Cabaret, Cafe de Paris. One place down in the old Royal Garden. Oh yes, I heard of that. And he was with us then. And then I think, who else was it? Some other band I worked with, Bud Scott. I can't think. I don't know whether it was Cook. No. I don't know whether it was Cook or not, but I think. Anyway, Bud was around in those years. Yeah. Yes, uh-huh. And I worked with him with a couple of bands around there.
See, Johnny Lindsey was the bass player on those Jelly Roll records. Yeah. Yes, yeah.

Did you ever work with him any place else? No, no. I owned a dance job several times. He played trombone too. Oh yes, that's right. Yes, uh-huh. Yes, I worked with him a number of times. Used to play, we used to play dances together too. Did you ever work with Roy Palmer on trombone? Roy Palmer? Yes. Uh, let's see, who wasn't a regular job? Where was it? I think that was on some dance work too.
He's one of my favorite tromboneers. He doesn't play now, but he was wonderful too.

Roy used to play when he would. When he'd feel like playing. He'd play. I haven't seen Roy for a long time. He's over on 51st and Wales, about. Uh-huh, uh-huh. Yeah, Roy used to play quite a bit of drum.
